children.text: This coconut plantation, cultivated by one family since the late 19th century, has been turned into a resort where in a single day you can enjoy a Filipino buffet lunch at bamboo tables below a waterfall with your feet in the water, along with a private museum, carabao-cart rides, and folk performances.
Villa Escudero is a coconut plantation resort on the border between Tiaong, Quezon, and San Pablo, Laguna, at the
91km
mark of the Maharlika Highway. The family estate once covered about 800 hectares, but in

more than half of it was developed into housing subdivisions, and the resort area today is about 40 hectares according to the official description. Don Placido Escudero and his wife bought the land in the
late 19th century
and established a sugarcane plantation (the official account says the
, the historical marker says
); their son Don Arsenio converted it into a coconut plantation in the
early 1900s
, and his children, Don Conrado (Ado) and his sisters, opened it to the public in
. The plantation is still a working farm, so the old Philippine countryside scene of carabao (water buffalo) pulling carts between endless rows of palm trees remains intact.

What made this place famous nationwide is the "Waterfall Restaurant." Bamboo tables are set just below a shallow waterfall spilling over the Labasin Dam, and guests dip their feet in the cool, ankle-deep water while eating Filipino food served on banana leaves. The sight of white water cascading behind the tables has appeared for decades, without fail, in postcards and travel guides introducing the Philippines.
The waterfall is actually a man-made dam. In
, Ciriaco Nadres, the land's previous owner, built an adobe-stone dam for irrigation; Placido Escudero and his wife, who bought the land, rebuilt it in stone and cement in
; and their son Arsenio and his wife modified it in

to serve both irrigation and hydropower, supplying electricity to the coconut processing plant and the mansion. Regarded as the first mini-hydroelectric dam in the Philippines, the dam (Don Placido Escudero Dam) received a historical marker in
, and the Arsenio Escudero Hydroelectric Power Plant building still stands beside the falls.

The Escudero family museum inside the resort is also worth seeing. Housed in a pink building resembling a Spanish colonial-era church, it's packed with the family's collection of religious icons (santos), silver altar ornaments, old coins and stamps, war relics, folk costumes, and taxidermy, and is known as one of the largest private collections in the Philippines.

With almost no physical demands and every activity contained within one compound, it especially suits trips with parents, families with young children, and expats hosting visitors from home. Unlike a flashy beach resort, it's a place to experience a slow, warm day of Philippine country life.

The highlight of the day tour. With your feet in the waterfall's water, enjoy a Filipino buffet of adobo, grilled fish, pancit, tropical fruit, and more. The water is cold and the floor is slippery, so aqua shoes are handy. The lunch buffet is served
Ride a cart pulled by water buffalo from the entrance to the plaza deep in the plantation. A local band riding along plays old Filipino songs on guitar and bandurria.
The family's collection, on display since

in a pink church-shaped building, offers plenty to see: statues of saints and religious art, the old altar of Quiapo Church, paintings by Amorsolo and Hidalgo, clothing worn by past presidents, and even World War II relics. Allow about
30–40 minutes
to look around with a guide's commentary. Photography and video are prohibited inside, and children aged 3–6 are not allowed in.

A folk dance show choreographed by National Artist of the Philippines Ramon Obusan, featuring traditional dances from various regions, such as tinikling, in which dancers leap between bamboo poles. Villa Escudero's own local troupe performs to live music every day,
Ride a bamboo raft along the Bulakin River, drifting slowly past palm-lined banks. Perfect for an unhurried afternoon outing.

The day tour includes use of the pools, which feature an infinity pool and a hot tub; the upper pool is for adults only. On the nature trails within the plantation, you can go bird-watching or rent a bike.

blocks.title: Photos of an old Philippine village scene

children.text: The scene of a bahay kubo (traditional bamboo house), a carabao, and palm trees comes even more alive in photos if you're dressed in traditional Filipino clothing.

A house museum: an old pink mansion built in Angeles, Pampanga, in the late 19th century, moved here piece by piece, and rebuilt. Filled with Escudero family keepsakes and genuine antique furniture, it offers a glimpse of a wealthy household from the Spanish colonial era.

From Manila, take SLEX down toward Calamba and Santo Tomas, pass through San Pablo town, and follow the Maharlika Highway toward Tiaong. It's about
90km
and takes
2–3 hours
; you can also go via the STAR Tollway through Lipa and San Pablo. Toll costs are about
one way.
The Santo Tomas–Tiaong section (about
) of SLEX Toll Road 4 (TR4) is under construction, with opening targeted for
November–December 2026
. Once it opens, the drive from Santo Tomas to Tiaong, which used to take about
2 hours
, is expected to shrink to around
30 minutes
, so check the latest announcements before you set off to see whether it has opened. When entering the resort parking lot, the driver must leave a driver's license or ID with the security guard.
From Buendia, Cubao, or PITX, take a bus (DLTB, JAC Liner, Jam Liner, etc.) bound for Lucena and ask to be let off at "Villa Escudero entrance." It takes about
2.5–3.5 hours
, with fares around
. From the entrance it's about a
5–10 minute
walk to the resort reception. For the return trip, flag down a Manila-bound bus on the road in front of the entrance.
JAC Liner is the easiest to catch, running buses to Lucena 24 hours a day every
15–30 minutes
from its Kamias (Cubao) and Buendia terminals. From PITX, JAM Liner and others run to Lucena roughly
. Students, seniors, and PWDs get a 20% fare discount on presenting an ID.

If you're heading straight from the airport, the easiest option is to take a Grab or taxi to the nearby PITX terminal and catch a Lucena-bound bus there. Rental or chartered cars take the NAIA Expressway and the Skyway down to SLEX, which takes about
2–3 hours
depending on traffic. On the day of your flight home, leave with plenty of time to spare for SLEX congestion.
Packages combining a Manila hotel pickup with day tour admission are sold for about
per person. The more people, the lower the transport cost per person, making it more economical.

Booking sites such as Klook also offer tours departing from Manila where you can choose a Korean-speaking guide. They usually leave Manila by van in the morning and return in the late afternoon, and private-vehicle options cost more per person.

items.title: Local transport and other starting points

children.text: If you are staying in San Pablo city, take a jeepney or bus toward Tiaong or Lucena and get off at the resort entrance right in front of the Laguna–Quezon provincial boundary arch; it takes about
20–30 minutes
. Grab cars can usually be booked in San Pablo, but they are hard to get when returning from the resort, so arrange your ride back in advance.
If coming from Lucena or Quezon, take a Manila-bound bus and get off at the same entrance, and from Batangas, going via the STAR Tollway through Lipa toward San Pablo puts you about
1–1.5 hours
away by car.
The best time to visit is the dry season,
November–May
December–February
in particular is cool, with daytime highs around
, making meals at the Waterfall Restaurant pleasant, while
March–May
is even more popular despite daytime highs of up to
, because the waterfall's water is refreshingly cool. However, rain in Tiaong is spread fairly evenly throughout the year, so even in the dry season, showers are frequent in
November–January
because of the northeast monsoon (amihan), with about 15 rainy days a month, and the driest period is
February–April
During the wet season (
June–October

), if it rains or the river rises, lunch is served at an indoor restaurant instead of the Waterfall Restaurant for safety. This can mean missing the day tour's key experience, so during the wet season it's best to check the forecast before picking a date. Raft operations may also be suspended right after a typhoon.
In nearby Lucban, Quezon Province, the Pahiyas Festival is held around
May 15
each year, when houses are decorated with rice wafers and farm produce. If you visit around
mid-May
, it's a great chance to combine the two destinations in one trip. Weekends, public holidays, and Holy Week draw large tour groups, so a weekday visit is recommended.

Accommodation at the resort consists of longhouses built of bamboo and wood in the style of traditional houses, and cottages along the Bulakin River. The overnight rate includes three meals (lunch, dinner, and breakfast) and resort activities, and the official rate is about
for two people (the riverside cottages without air conditioning are the cheapest, and the Presidential Suite is the most expensive). Each extra person costs

for vehicle parking, and a

resort entrance fee. At night the atmosphere is rural, with frogs and insects calling, so don't expect a quiet city-style hotel. To save money, you can stay at a budget or mid-range hotel in San Pablo city, about
20–30 minutes
away by car (about
per night).

Lunch at the Waterfall Restaurant is a buffet of Filipino home cooking, with chicken adobo, grilled tilapia, pancit canton, lumpia, steamed rice, and tropical fruit such as bananas and mangoes. There's hardly any spicy food, so it suits children's tastes too. Dinner (
) and breakfast (
) buffets for overnight guests are served at the Coconut Pavilion, and coffee is available at Cafe Indigo. Outside food and drinks are not allowed without prior arrangement and a corkage fee.

For local food, the buko pie sold along the national highway in San Pablo and Los Baños is famous, and the longganisa (garlicky sausage) of Lucban, Quezon, and pancit habhab, eaten by hand from a banana leaf, are well worth trying. Fittingly for a coconut plantation, fresh buko juice (young coconut water) is a must too. The Artikulo souvenir shop inside the resort sells local crafts, and at the Ugu Bigyan pottery garden in Lusacan, Tiaong, a little farther from Villa Escudero toward Lucena, you can browse the workshop and pottery shop (the garden restaurant is by reservation only).
It's safest to book the day tour in advance through the official online shop (shop.villaescudero.com). On weekends and public holidays, walk-in tickets can sell out early.
Operating hours are usually
8 AM to 5 PM
. Activities after entry can be done in any order, but the cultural show runs only at set times, so check the schedule when you enter.
If you get to the Waterfall Restaurant before half past
, there are fewer people and photos come out clean. After
, it gets crowded with tour groups.
Shorts, sandals, or aqua shoes are comfortable to wear. Your clothes can get wet from the waterfall, so bring a change of clothes.

Only proper swimwear such as spandex swimsuits, board shorts, and rash guards is allowed in the pools; cotton clothing with zippers is not. Children aged 7 and under must be accompanied by an adult at all times, and day tour guests can rent lockers to store their belongings.

The senior and PWD discounts apply only to holders of Philippine government-issued senior or PWD IDs, and you must show your ID at the reception desk on arrival. The discounted rate applies only to regular rates and cannot be combined with promotions.
Both cash and cards are accepted, but the small shops on the plantation often take cash only.
If you're coming by bus, check the last return departure time in advance. Once the sun sets, it gets harder to flag down a bus on the road by the entrance.
The day tour adult rate is
Monday to Thursday,
Friday to Sunday, and
on public holidays, with ages 3–6 at about half. Discount promotions sometimes appear during the rainy season of
July–September
, so check the latest rates on the
official day tour booking page

Pets are not allowed, and drone flying and commercial photography or filming require written permission from the resort. Overnight bookings can be changed or canceled without penalty up to 72 hours before arrival.

All guests must sign a waiver on entry, and the resort is not responsible for accidents resulting from failure to follow safety rules and warning signs. Be sure to follow staff instructions at the Waterfall Restaurant, on the bamboo rafts, and in the pools.

The floor of the Waterfall Restaurant is very slippery because of moss. Elderly visitors should always hold someone's hand when moving around, and keep an eye on children so they don't run around in the water.
On days with heavy rain, the waterfall meal may be canceled for safety, and in that case it's usually replaced with an indoor meal rather than a refund.
Carabao are gentle animals, but they can be startled if you suddenly approach or touch them from behind. Follow the staff's instructions when riding the cart.
There are a lot of mosquitoes around the plantation. Especially at dusk, bring long clothing and insect repellent to guard against dengue.
The Maharlika Highway has heavy truck traffic. Take extra care when getting off a bus or crossing the road.

Some travel agencies have posted notices that the main Escudero Museum is closed indefinitely for renovation (the official website still lists the museum visit as an included item in 2026). If the museum is the reason for your visit, check with the resort (info@villaescudero.com) before booking whether it's open, and if it's closed, ask whether you can book a separate tour of the Casa Consuelo Mansion Museum.
